candidates.paraphrase: Jeff Bezos/Amazon (post One Medical acquisition) will not be the visionary that transforms US healthcare; nor will Elon Musk; the eventual 'Elon Musk of Healthcare' will be an experienced outsider. Framed as tongue-in-cheek 'prophecies'.
candidates.resolution_hint: Amazon One Medical performance and strategy reporting 2023-2026

candidates.resolution_hint: Tesla market share, Boring Company tunnel deployments 2023-2026

candidates.title: Will 988 Be a Joke in Your Town?
candidates.quote: We call bullshit that any of our patients will be meaningfully impacted in the near term by this change.
candidates.paraphrase: The launch of the 988 crisis line will not meaningfully change outcomes or access for psychiatric patients in the near term. (Co-signed by Owen Muir and Carlene MacMillan.)
candidates.resolution_hint: SAMHSA 988 performance data; RAND/JAMA evaluations of 988 impact 2023-2025

candidates.title: Will 988 Be a Joke in Your Town?
candidates.quote: While this initial funding push will help, serious doubts exist if it will be sustained or enough to meet increased demand caused by publicizing the new 988 number.
candidates.paraphrase: Federal 988 funding ($282M in 2021, $150M in 2022) will likely not be sustained or sufficient to meet the demand created by publicizing the number.
candidates.resolution_hint: Federal 988 appropriations FY2023-FY2026; state 988 telecom fee legislation; 988 answer-rate data

candidates.title: Will 988 Be a Joke in Your Town?
candidates.quote: 988 can save lives too if more effort and funding is directed at what happens when the callers needing more help than the line on its own hang up the phone.
candidates.paraphrase: Conditional: 988 will save lives only if funding and effort go to downstream crisis services (mobile response, follow-up care) rather than the hotline alone.
candidates.resolution_hint: 988 outcome studies; state crisis-continuum funding reports

candidates.title: Cerebral: Vastly Exceeding the Standard of Care?

candidates.title: Post Roe Crisis: Mandatory Malpractice Creates Problems for Health Care
candidates.quote: This is only the first shot. ERISA is next. ... Enforcement is coming. This is not a drill.
candidates.paraphrase: After the DOJ EMTALA suit against Idaho/Ohio, federal ERISA fiduciary enforcement (Department of Labor) against employer plans in abortion-ban states will follow.
candidates.resolution_hint: DOL/DOJ ERISA enforcement actions related to abortion coverage 2022-2026 (none known)

candidates.title: Post Roe Crisis: Mandatory Malpractice Creates Problems for Health Care
candidates.quote: Turning back the clock fifty years on Roe will lead to similarly catastrophic outcomes—physician shortages, dead patients beyond those seeking abortions, and tax liability for large employers in impacted states.
candidates.paraphrase: Overturning Roe will cause physician shortages, patient deaths beyond abortion seekers, and employer tax liability in states that ban abortion.
candidates.resolution_hint: AAMC residency application data for ban states; ProPublica maternal death investigations 2023-2024; IRS guidance on employer plans (none)

candidates.title: Post Roe Crisis: Mandatory Malpractice Creates Problems for Health Care
candidates.quote: So, as soon as patients sue doctors who can’t follow established medical guidelines, doctors will flee those states.
candidates.paraphrase: Conditional: once malpractice suits hit doctors barred from following standard of care in abortion-ban states, malpractice carriers will not insure them and doctors will leave those states.
candidates.resolution_hint: Physician workforce reports in Idaho, Texas, Tennessee 2023-2025 (OB/GYN departures)

candidates.title: Post Roe Crisis: Mandatory Malpractice Creates Problems for Health Care
candidates.quote: Now, every employer who has any employees in any state that bans abortion owes the IRS on every penny they spend on health benefits for their employees.
candidates.paraphrase: Employers with employees in abortion-ban states will lose the ERISA tax exemption on health benefits because their plans cannot cover all medically necessary care.
candidates.resolution_hint: IRS/Treasury guidance on employer health benefit tax status after Dobbs (none issued); ERISA case law

candidates.title: Post Roe Crisis: Mandatory Malpractice Creates Problems for Health Care
candidates.quote: There are a hell of a lot of lawsuits coming. This will be catastrophic for most patients, their employers, doctors– and even insurance conglomerates.
candidates.paraphrase: A wave of lawsuits will follow Dobbs and will be catastrophic for patients, employers, doctors, and insurers.
candidates.resolution_hint: Post-Dobbs litigation trackers (Brennan Center, KFF) 2022-2026
